newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Jet fuel trades around $25.00/bbl.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Jet fuel trades around $25.00/bbl.

text.p: The quiet jet fuel market was given some boost on Tuesday when a Singapore trader, who has been very active in the gas oil market, bought two jet cargoes at around $25.00 per barrel, traders said.
The purchases from a European major at $25.00 and $25.40 for end April/early May liftings, provided some support to the sleepy market which was weighed down by poor regional demand.
The last deal was done on April 3 when a Chinese trader sold a cargo to a US trader at $25.90 per barrel.
Traders said the jet fuel would be blended into the gas oil pool to cut the cost of the more expensive gas oil.
The jet fuel market was also concerned that Taiwan might not issue a jet fuel tender for June requirements.
Abu Dhabi National Oil Co (ADNOC) has issued a tender to sell 25,000 tonnes of jet fuel for mid May lifting, on a free-on-board (fob) basis.

Traders said ADNOC might not have awarded its previous sale tender for April lifting as the offers were too low, around 30-40 cents per barrel below MidEast spot quotes fob. But MidEast sources said the tender has been awarded but did not disclose the price or the buyer.
The Singapore trader and its sister company also continued to buy gas oil on Tuesday bringing their total over two weeks to 3.5 million barrels.
The sellers were a European major at $27.30 for April 30-May 4 and a Swiss trader at $27.00 for May 6-10 lifting.
The two traders have so far bought nearly 14 million barrels since March 3 and has not shown signs of stopping.
India's diesel tender for June delivery, which was expected to be issued on Tuesday has been delayed until Thursday or Friday, Indian sources said.
Gas oil swaps slipped 30 cents for May and 15 cents for June to $25.50/$25.65 and $24.50/$24.60 respectively as the paper drifted in directionless trading.
